reads.label: ### ### **THE BOUNDARY PARAGRAPH, WHOLE**
reads.text: **The boundary is a local-to-global interchange.** The step from "consistent at every finite modulus" to "holds globally" (positive global density) interchanges a per-modulus quantifier with a global one — a local-to-global passage, not a mechanical corollary. The programme has exactly this shape compiled, in the RH setting, as a bracket in `SIDE-lv-conservation` v0.8.0 (version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21436280; concept 10.5281/zenodo.21433177): the unrestricted commutation of the two quantifiers is **false** as a theorem (`T3.T3doubleprime_general_commutation_fails`, an explicit countermodel), and it **closes only under a shared witness** (`T3.T3prime_shared_witness`). For twin primes, Goldbach, and Sophie Germain, the shared witness *is* the analytic content — the Hardy-Littlewood asymptotic, the circle-method lower bound, the sieve density (M3/M4/M5). The same bracket in the RH setting is developed in *The Unconditional Surround of ξ* (`phase1.5/proofs/THE_UNCONDITIONAL_SURROUND.md`).

reads.label: ### the residue named for twin primes (M3)
reads.text: The analytic requirement is named as M3: the Hardy-Littlewood asymptotic $\pi_2(N) \sim 2C_2 N/(\log N)^2 \to \infty$, formalized against Mathlib. The finite-modulus no-conspiracy does not reach this statement — the density lower bound is the whole of the remaining weight.

reads.label: ### the residue named for Goldbach (M4)
reads.text: The analytic requirement is named as M4: the circle method bounding the representation count $r(n)$ from below by a positive quantity for every even $n \geq 4$. The finite-modulus no-conspiracy does not reach this statement — the representation lower bound is the whole of the remaining weight.
